newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Ceval says bought 150,000 tns U.S. soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Ceval says bought 150,000 tns U.S. soybeans.

text.p: Brazilian food processor Ceval Alimentos said it had bought 150,000 tonnes of U.S. new crop soybeans for shipment in October, November and December.
"It is five cargoes of 30,000 tonnes each, one for October, two for November and two for December," said Charles Van Der Heyde, director of external sales.
Meanwhile, negotiations to sell 40,000 tonnes soymeal to an unidentified U.S. buyer had fallen through, he said.
"We didn't close the deal. Cargill is going to import beans and they probably have enough beans there now," he said.
Ceval's purchase of U.S. soybeans was concluded in mid-May, Van Der Heyde said. He declined to disclose the identity of the seller and the price, saying only it was based on premiums at the time.

The beans were bought FOB and will be shipped from the Gulf of Mexico to Ceval's facilities at the southern port of Sao Francisco do Sul, although they could be resold to a U.S. buyer if it turns out that Ceval has enough supply, he added.
"It is above our needs for Sao Francisco do Sul," Van Der Heyde said. "We may resell the product there in the U.S."
Ceval usually buys most of its soybean imports from Paraguay, but supply there starts to dwindle in November and December, he said.
